newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent erases early losses, gas oil ends firm.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent erases early losses, gas oil ends firm.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures clawed back early losses in late afternoon trade on Wednesday as a wave of profit-taking petered out and dealers sought cover ahead of a long weekend in the United States.
Aug Brent shed five cents to $18.75 a barrel by 1640 GMT, three cents off the session high but well above the $18.50 low.
After running up smartly on Tuesday in anticipation of bullish U.S. inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), modest losses had been expected from the open.
"The market needed a correction and it got that overnight after the APIs," said a broker.
"There was fairly good selling this morning but the buyers have come back in and any break above yesterday's high (of $18.85) would generate fresh impetus," he said.
IPE gas oil also benefited from the rebound, the prompt July contract losing just 25 cents to close at $167.50 a tonne after dipping as low as $166.
Brokers said a firm spot market for gas oil in Europe, where heating oil and diesel differentials have been strengthening steadily since the start of the week, gave futures support.
API data, confirmed Wednesday by U.S. Department of Energy figures, showed crude and gasoline stocks fell last week.
European crude markets are also tight, helped by continuing uncertainty over the date for a resumption of Iraqi exports, but some dealers saw little room for further gains.

"Once a definite date for Iraq's return is confirmed people will start to focus on that. I'm not convinced the market can sustain these levels," said a broker, adding that the U.S. inventory data also showed a big build in distillate stocks.

U.S. markets are shut on Friday for the Independence Day holiday, seen as the peak of the gasoline season after which traders usually switch their attention to winter heating oil demand. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44PE crude
